canvas-01.description: The lower half of sheet 1 is a map at 50 feet to an inch of six blocks at the northwest edge of built-up Carlstadt; the upper half of the sheet, left out of this part, carries the key map of the town, the street and specials index, the water and fire department notes, the title cartouche and the legend. The map lies between Division Avenue along the bottom edge and Central Avenue across the middle, with the cross streets Garden (on the left edge, drawn at a slight angle to the grid), Lincoln, Union and Washington (on the right edge). Blocks 201, 204 and 205 lie between Division and Central Avenues, and blocks 202, 203 and 206 beyond Central Avenue, cut off at the top by the heavy line under the key map. The area is thinly built, with a few frame dwellings of one and a half to two storeys on large lots, a brick house, and a small paint shop in block 206. The only industry is Smith and Nichols, makers of candles and wax compounds, which fills the corner of Central Avenue and Lincoln in block 201: casting, melting, finishing, drawing and moulding rooms, a packing room, a bleach house, storage sheds, a grease house with kettle, a cable shed with melting kettles, and long rows of bleaching tables drawn in dashed outline. Six-inch water pipes run in Central Avenue and Garden. The legend box of the sheet sits in the top left of the map over block 202 and is masked out.
notes: The upper half of the sheet (key map, index, legend) is not georeferenced; only the map below the heavy dividing line is.
Smith and Nichols, manufacturers of candles and wax compounds, at Central Avenue and Lincoln.
Blocks north of Central Avenue have no junction on the sheet beyond Central Avenue, so their placement is extrapolated from the Central Avenue and Division Avenue rows.

map: sheet 1. Upper half is the key map of the town, the street and specials index, notes and legend (not georeferenced); lower half is a 50 ft map of blocks 201-206: Central Av, Division Av, Garden, Lincoln, Union, Washington. One part (config canvas-01), legend box notched out of the mask.

sheet-2-1.description: The main map of sheet 2, at 50 feet to an inch, covers the southwest corner of Carlstadt between Division Avenue at the top and Hoboken (now Hoboken Road) at the bottom, where the dash-dot line of the Borough of East Rutherford follows the street. Garden runs down the middle of the sheet at a slight angle to the grid, and Lincoln runs along the right edge, marked as not opened between Division Avenue and Broad. Broad crosses from Garden to Lincoln. West of Garden, block 101 is mostly open: ball grounds with bleachers, a few dwellings and coops, a saloon on Hoboken, and the car barn of the Public Service Corporation of N.J. (storage of cars, 18 ft to the eaves) near the tracks. The Erie Railroad (Bergen County Railroad) crosses the lower left corner of the sheet on several tracks. East of Garden, block 103 holds the Franco American Chemical Co., manufacturers of pharmaceutical specialties, with a distilling room, filling and packing rooms, an office, store houses and a boiler house, and a few dwellings along Division Avenue. Block 102, between Broad, Garden, Lincoln and Hoboken, is taken up by Sharg Bros., manufacturers of silk, with a long weaving and winding mill, a machine shop, a boiler house and coal shed, and some dwellings and sheds. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches run in Garden, Broad and Hoboken. The upper left corner of the sheet is given to two insets, drawn as separate parts.
notes: Lincoln is marked 'Not Opened' between Division Avenue and Broad.
Franco American Chemical Co. (pharmaceutical specialties) and Sharg Bros. silk mill.
Car barn of the Public Service Corporation of N.J. by the Erie Railroad at Hoboken.

map, 50 ft, three parts. Part 1 (main): Division Av to Hoboken, Garden (angled) to Lincoln, Broad; Franco American Chemical Co., Sharg Bros. silk mill, Public Service car barn, Erie (Bergen County) RR. Part 2 (inset, upper left): block 207, Sixth to Seventh, Berry Av to Division Av, Lincoln Public School; Berry and Division drawn 25 ft wide. Part 3 (inset, left): Carlstadt Consumers Ice Co. at Division Av and Eleventh by the Erie (N.J. & N.Y.) RR; Eleventh no longer exists, anchored on the rail crossing.

sheet-2-2.description: This inset in the upper left corner of sheet 2, at 50 feet to an inch, shows a single block, number 207, at the eastern edge of Carlstadt: the block between Sixth on the left and Seventh on the right, from Berry Avenue at the top to Division Avenue at the bottom. Neither Berry Avenue nor Division Avenue is drawn in full; Division Avenue is drawn 25 feet wide here, with the outline of the next block beyond it, and the inset is closed by a heavy border along Seventh and below Division Avenue. The northern half of the block has a few frame dwellings, a saloon at the corner of Berry Avenue and Seventh, a barn, a chicken house and green houses with a hot water boiler, and a stone cutting shed. The southern half is taken up by the Lincoln Public School, a two-storey brick building with a boiler room in the basement, marked as drawn from plans. A six-inch water pipe runs in Seventh.
notes: Lincoln Public School, drawn from plans.
Division Avenue and Berry Avenue are drawn about 25 ft wide here against about 45 to 50 ft today; both were given that width for the detector. Sixth / Berry Avenue was hand-picked.

map, 50 ft, three parts. Part 3 (inset, left): Carlstadt Consumers Ice Co. at Division Av and Eleventh by the Erie (N.J. & N.Y.) RR; Eleventh no longer exists, anchored on the rail crossing.

sheet-2-3.description: This small inset on the left side of sheet 2, at 50 feet to an inch, shows the plant of the Carlstadt Consumers Ice Co. at the southeastern end of Carlstadt, on the block between Eleventh and the Erie Railroad (New Jersey and New York Railroad) on the north side of Division Avenue, which is drawn 31 feet wide. The ice company's building is a single brick and cement block structure with storage, an ice machine and freezing tanks, a boiler with a 90 ft iron chimney, and a defective cement block wall. West of Eleventh there is one frame dwelling. The railroad runs on a double line up the right side of the inset. The outlines of the blocks across Division Avenue, on sheets 8 and 9, are sketched along the edges.
notes: Eleventh no longer exists between Division Avenue and Broad; the part is anchored on the crossing of Division Avenue and the railroad (today the Pascack Valley Line) at the atlas scale and the rotation of the other sheets, with one derived point. Low confidence.
Carlstadt Consumers Ice Co., freezing tanks and ice machine.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers six blocks of central Carlstadt at 50 feet to an inch, between Division Avenue at the top and Hoboken (now Hoboken Road) at the bottom, where the dash-dot line of the Borough of East Rutherford runs along the street. Broad Street crosses the middle of the sheet, and the cross streets are, from left to right, Lincoln, Union, Washington, Jefferson and Madison; Lincoln, on the left edge, is marked as not opened between Division Avenue and Broad. The blocks are numbered 103 and 102 (Lincoln to Union), 104 and 105 (Union to Washington), 107 and 106 (Washington to Jefferson) and 208 and 108 (Jefferson to Madison). The area is residential, with frame dwellings of one and a half to two and a half storeys on narrow lots, a few brick houses and flats, and coops and sheds behind. Small industries are scattered through it: the Bergen Manufacturing Co. machine shop and C. Heger, manufacturer of pearl buttons, both run by gasoline engines, on the blocks north of Broad; Wm. Braddac, manufacturer of pearl buttons, at Broad and Lincoln; the Julius Koch Co. carpenter and machine works with lumber storage on Broad between Union and Washington; and two yards of Kastner and Semper, masons and contractors, one with a cement block making shed and an open area where cement blocks and sand are stored, the other with wagon sheds and storage of masons' material between Washington and Jefferson. A grocery stands at Broad and Washington. Six-inch water pipes are drawn in Broad, Union, Jefferson, Madison and Hoboken. The margins carry the outlines of the adjoining sheets 1, 2, 4 and 5.
notes: Lincoln is marked 'Not Opened' between Division Avenue and Broad.
The street printed 'Hoboken' is Hoboken Road today; it is the borough line with East Rutherford.
Broad is drawn 60 ft wide, Division Avenue 40 ft, the cross streets 50 ft.
map, 50 ft: Division Av, Broad, Hoboken (East Rutherford line); Lincoln (not opened), Union, Washington, Jefferson, Madison. Pearl button makers, Kastner & Semper.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the northern edge of Carlstadt at 50 feet to an inch: three rows of blocks between Passaic Avenue at the top, which carries the dash-dot line of the Borough of Woodridge, and Division Avenue at the bottom, crossed by Summit Avenue and Central Avenue. The cross streets are, from left to right, Washington (on the left edge), Jefferson, Madison, Monroe and First (on the right edge). The blocks are numbered 209, 36 and 35 (Washington to Jefferson), 37, 38 and 39 (Jefferson to Madison), 41, 1 and 40 (Madison to Monroe) and 45, 2 and 5 (Monroe to First). Most of the sheet is open lots with scattered frame dwellings, flats and a few brick houses. Two large pleasure grounds take up the middle of it: Wagner's Union Park, between Summit and Central Avenues and Madison and Monroe, with a hotel and bar, a dance pavilion with a stage and basement dining room, and bowling alleys; and Fink's Mt. Pleasant Park, on Division Avenue between Jefferson and Madison, with bowling alleys, a dance pavilion, an amusement hall with bar and basement dining room, and a stage. The Hackensack Water Co. has two circular reservoirs, with a combined capacity of 1,000,000 gallons, on Summit Avenue at Madison, fed by 12-inch water pipes in Summit Avenue, Passaic Avenue and Monroe. Block 40 has a small sawing shed with an electric motor, and block 5 a Sunday school. The street widths are marked 50 feet, with Passaic Avenue 25 feet on this side of the borough line.
notes: Passaic Avenue on this sheet is Fritsch Avenue today; Washington, Jefferson, Madison and Monroe meet it at the Carlstadt and Wood-Ridge line.
Hackensack Water Co. reservoirs, combined capacity 1,000,000 gallons, at Summit Avenue and Madison.
The junction of Summit Avenue and Washington, at the left edge of the sheet, was excluded: the detector paired the sheet border with a block line there.

map, 50 ft: Passaic Av (now Fritsch Avenue, Wood-Ridge line), Summit Av, Central Av, Division Av; Washington, Jefferson, Madison, Monroe, First. Hackensack Water Co. reservoirs, Wagner's Union Park, Fink's Mt. Pleasant Park.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers eight blocks of central Carlstadt at 50 feet to an inch, between Division Avenue at the top and Hoboken (now Hoboken Road) at the bottom, where the dash-dot line of the Borough of East Rutherford runs along the street. Broad Street crosses the middle of the sheet, and the cross streets are, from left to right, Madison (on the left edge), Monroe, First, Second and Third (on the right edge). The blocks are numbered 42 and 43 (Madison to Monroe), 6 and 8 (Monroe to First), 7 and 9 (First to Second) and 20 and 19 (Second to Third). This is the busiest part of the town: frame dwellings and flats line every street, with groceries, saloons, confectioners, a barber, a drug store, an undertaker and a moving picture show along Broad Street and Division Avenue. Public buildings include the Carlstadt Baptist Church on Madison, Hose Co. No. 2 with its hose carriage on Division Avenue, a park with a stage and balcony hall between Monroe and First, Turn Halle with bowling alleys on Broad between Monroe and First, and Concordia Hall between Madison and Monroe. Industry is represented by the Cragin Mfg. Co., makers of hatters' glaze and specialties, a mill with drying racks at Broad and First; the bottling works of P. W. Kessler and of Wm. Umbach on Second; Henry Noll, maker of book binding bands; a machine shop doing electro plating and metal novelties and a vacant factory near Broad and Madison; and a pool room and bowling alleys at Broad and Second. Water pipes of 6 and 12 inches run in all the streets. The top margin repeats the outlines of sheets 4 and 6, the side margins those of sheets 3 and 7.
notes: Division Avenue is drawn about 46 to 48 ft wide here; its far side is only sketched as the outline of sheets 4 and 6, and the detector paired its near edge with a lot line about 47 ft inside the blocks. The mask was set along the Division Avenue centreline and the Division Avenue junctions were excluded; the part is placed on the Broad Street and Hoboken rows.
Cragin Mfg. Co., makers of hatters' glaze and specialties, at Broad and First.
Turn Halle and Concordia Hall, both with stages, and a park with a stage and balcony hall.

map, 50 ft: Division Av, Broad, Hoboken; Madison, Monroe, First, Second, Third. Cragin Mfg Co., Turn Halle, Concordia Hall, Baptist church. Division Av drawn 46-48 ft and its far side only sketched; Division junctions excluded and mask set on its centreline.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the northern part of Carlstadt at 50 feet to an inch, from Passaic Avenue at the top, where the dash-dot line of the Borough of Woodridge runs along the street, down across Summit Avenue and Central Avenue to Division Avenue at the bottom. The cross streets are, from left to right, First (on the left edge), Second and Third, with Hackensack running at an angle down the right-hand side of the sheet. The blocks are numbered 46, 47 and 48 between Passaic and Summit, 3, 44, 49 and 50 between Summit and Central, and 4, 21, 22 and 50 between Central and Division. The district is thinly built: most lots hold frame dwellings, with large empty lots in blocks 47, 48 and 49 and a street east of Hackensack marked Not Opened. The main buildings are the Summer Garden with a pool room and bar on Second near Summit, a coffin shop with an electric motor and a lumber shed in block 47, the Theo. Goers factory, makers of ladies' undergarments (underwear factory with a gas engine), at Central and Second, and the First German Evangelical Church with its Sunday school on Division Avenue between Second and Third. Block 49 has a cement block flats building on Central Avenue, and there is a small frame stable on Hackensack. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches run in the streets. A few lots beyond Passaic Avenue are drawn at the top, with Hill Street at the top right corner; the sheet title and a compass rose sit in block 50, and the scale bar in block 22.
notes: Passaic Avenue is today's Fritsch Avenue (OpenStreetMap); it is drawn about 25 ft wide with the Woodridge borough line along its south side.
The street marked Not Opened east of Hackensack, between Summit and Central, corresponds to the modern Berry Avenue; it was left out of the control.
Theo. Goers, manufacturer of ladies' undergarments, at Central and Second.
First German Evangelical Church and Sunday school on Division Avenue.

map, 50 ft: Passaic Av (now Fritsch Avenue, Woodridge line, drawn 25 ft), Summit Av, Central Av, Division Av; First, Second, Third, Hackensack (angled). Theo. Goers underwear factory, First German Evangelical Church, summer garden. A street marked 'Not Opened' east of Hackensack (Berry Avenue today) not used.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the commercial centre of Carlstadt at 50 feet to an inch, between Division Avenue at the top and Hoboken at the bottom, where the dash-dot line of the Borough of East Rutherford runs along the street. Broad crosses the middle of the sheet and Small runs between Fourth and Hackensack below it. The cross streets are, from left to right, Third (on the left edge), Fourth, Hackensack (running at an angle down the sheet), Fifth, Lilac Lane (angled, from Hoboken up to Broad) and Sixth (on the right edge). Division Avenue between Fifth and Sixth is drawn in dashed lines and marked Not Opened. The blocks are numbered 23, 24, 25 and 26 above Broad and 18, 17, 16, 15 and 14 below it. Hackensack is the main shopping street, lined with a confectioner, wall paper, dry goods, tailor, bakery and restaurant, undertaker, Chinese laundry, barber, meat markets, house furnishings, jewelry, groceries, saloons, a hardware store and a cigar maker. Larger premises include the greenhouses of Jacob H. Ullmann, florist, on Third; the saloon and bottling shop of Theo. Otto; the Van Diemen Engraving and Type Mfg. Co. and the Boiling Springs Bottling Co. (cement block construction) on Fourth; an ice cream factory; a bank and an insurance office at Broad and Hackensack; and P. Zimmermann's hall with a stage, dining room and bowling alleys, a semicircular bandstand area and a retaining wall, between Hackensack and Lilac Lane. Public buildings are Carlstadt Public School No. 1 and the Fire Department Fire House No. 1 and Borough Hall, with a bell tower and hose tower, on Third below Broad, and Fire Dept. Hose Co. No. 3 on Sixth. A post office stands on Fourth near Division Avenue, and a small underwear factory on Small.
notes: Division Avenue between Fifth and Sixth is marked Not Opened; the 6th Street / Division Avenue junction was not detected.
Broad bends at Sixth; Lilac Lane meets Broad at the Sixth Street junction (today one node: 6th Street / Broad Street / Lilac Lane).
Carlstadt Public School No. 1 and the Fire Department house with Borough Hall on Third below Broad.
P. Zimmermann's hall with bowling alleys, Van Diemen Engraving and Type Mfg. Co., Boiling Springs Bottling Co., Jacob H. Ullmann greenhouses.
A correction date of 8-10-09 is written at the bottom right corner.

map, 50 ft: Division Av, Broad, Small, Hoboken; Third, Fourth, Hackensack (angled), Fifth, Lilac Lane, Sixth. Division between Fifth and Sixth 'Not Opened'. Carlstadt Public School No. 1, fire house and Borough Hall, Zimmermann hall, Van Diemen engraving, Boiling Springs Bottling Co. Lower right (Fifth to Sixth below Broad) has no control of its own.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers eight blocks of eastern Carlstadt at 50 feet to an inch, between Division Avenue at the top and Hoboken at the bottom, where the dash-dot line of the Borough of East Rutherford runs along the street. Broad crosses the middle of the sheet, and the cross streets are, from left to right, Sixth (on the left edge), Seventh, Eighth, Ninth and Tenth (on the right edge). The blocks are numbered 28, 52, 53 and 56 above Broad and 27, 51, 54 and 55 below it. Division Avenue is drawn only about 25 ft wide here, with the outlines of the blocks of sheet 2 sketched across it. The district is mostly frame dwellings and flats on large, partly empty lots. Block 52 holds the Carlstadt Cemetery along Division Avenue and Mueller's Casino, a saloon with bowling alleys, at its Seventh Street side. Block 28 has the greenhouses of Mrs. W. Rummler, florist, a stone cutting shop with storage and a tool house, and flats; a bakery with a bake house and oven stands at Broad and Sixth. Below Broad there is a small underwear factory with an electric motor at Broad and Seventh, a tin shop on Seventh, groceries, a confectioner, a barber and a smoke house. The largest works is S. Klaber and Co., marble works and bronze foundry, at Hoboken and Tenth, with iron-clad sawing and polishing sheds, a planing room, a rubbing bed, a bronze foundry, a blacksmith shop, a cutting, carving and polishing building, a wagon and marble shed, and storage of plaster, excelsior and oils. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches run in the streets, and a fire alarm box stands on Hoboken at Ninth.
notes: Division Avenue is drawn about 25 ft wide between Sixth and Tenth (the detector paired its block edge with the sketched outline of sheet 2; residuals 0.4 to 0.8 m).
S. Klaber and Co. marble works and bronze foundry at Hoboken and Tenth.
Mueller's Casino with bowling alleys; Mrs. W. Rummler, florist, greenhouses.
Correction dates of 8-15-09 are written at the bottom right corner.
map, 50 ft: Division Av (drawn about 25 ft), Broad, Hoboken; Sixth, Seventh, Eighth, Ninth, Tenth. Carlstadt Cemetery, Mueller's Casino, S. Klaber & Co. marble works and bronze foundry.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the eastern edge of Carlstadt at 50 feet to an inch, between Division Avenue at the top and Hoboken at the bottom, where the dash-dot line of the Borough of East Rutherford runs along the street. Broad crosses the middle of the sheet, and the cross streets are, from left to right, Tenth (near the left edge), Eleventh, Twelfth (below Broad) and Thirteenth, which is a 20 ft lane north of Broad and a 50 ft street south of it. The double track of the Erie Railroad (N.J. and N.Y. R.R.) runs diagonally down the sheet between Eleventh and Thirteenth, with a siding into a coal yard, and the Carlstadt Depot, a small passenger station, stands beside the tracks at Hoboken. The blocks, numbered 211, 109 and 110 above Broad and 210 and 212 below it, are thinly built with scattered frame dwellings and large empty lots. Industry includes the Nehr Sanitary Bed Co. on Eleventh (machine shop, polishing, assembling and lacquer rooms, with a brass foundry and storage); the machine shop with two electric motors of August Gerecke and a factory with an electric motor marked not running, in block 109 beside the railroad; G. Depken and Sons coal pockets with a belt conveyor elevator, on Thirteenth; a casket factory with sawing, planing and bench work on Twelfth; a wood working and blacksmith shop with an engine in block 210; and a carpenter shop on Division Avenue. A marble shed and coal bin stand on Hoboken at Tenth, and there are a barber, a confectioner, an insurance office and a shed along Hoboken. A ruined dwelling stands on Division Avenue east of Eleventh.
notes: Eleventh no longer exists between Division Avenue and Hoboken; there is no 11th Street here in OpenStreetMap.

Twelfth runs along the west side of the Erie tracks; the modern 12th Street / Broad Street node lies about 10 m from the modern rail crossing, against about 3 m on the sheet, so 12th Street was left out of the control.
Thirteenth north of Broad is drawn as a 20 ft lane; the modern 13th Street junctions carry residuals of about 2 m.
The Erie Railroad (N.J. and N.Y. R.R.) is today's Pascack Valley Line; the Broad Street crossing was detected and the Division Avenue crossing hand-picked.
Nehr Sanitary Bed Co., G. Depken and Sons coal pockets, a casket factory and the Carlstadt Depot.

map, 50 ft: Division Av, Broad, Hoboken; Tenth, Eleventh (gone today), Twelfth, Thirteenth (a 20 ft lane north of Broad); Erie (N.J. & N.Y.) RR, now the Pascack Valley Line, with the Carlstadt depot. Nehr Sanitary Bed Co., G. Depken & Sons coal pockets, a casket factory. 12th Street left out (its modern node does not match the drawn spacing to the rail). Division / Erie crossing hand-picked.
